fields.quoted_span: Housing providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
fields.note: The requirement is tracked closely, including the direct-relation test and the weighing of nature and severity and time elapsed, as well as tenant screening companies being covered.

fields.quoted_span: Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
fields.note: The substantive prohibitions are supported. The 'effective Jan. 1, 2020' element does not appear in D016. It comes from another document, DX07.
D016 gives no effective date or adoption year for the criminal history rules. The 2020-01-01 date relies on DX07, which is outside this document.

fields.quoted_span: Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
fields.note: The present-tense FAQ language describes the rule as currently operative, which is consistent with in_force.

fields.quoted_span: The Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) covers the sale, rental, or occupancy of most housing accommodations in California, including single-family homes, multi-family homes, condominiums, apartments
fields.note: The statewide scope, the covered entities including tenant screening companies, and the owner-occupied rent-to-one-person exemption are all supported. The exemption text is 'When an owner is occupying a home and is renting to one additional person, the owner may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics.'

D016 does not mention Cal. Code Regs. tit. 2, § 12264 or any of the aliases (§§ 12265, 12266). It refers only to CRD's criminal history factsheet and FAQ and to FEHA generally. The review note also concedes that the section numbers are unverified.
